gate_1_return_path_redrawn.claim: the coupled step is the monolithic step within the field's solve's line, both dtypes, every draw's two partners reading each other above float32's line

prediction.unit: relative (field, force, twist, pressure, flux), float64; float32 [1e-7, 2e-3]
prediction.basis: measured-before (the first draw's 30 seeds) and derived: closer bodies change the cross terms' size, not the CG's tolerance the line carries
prediction.why: every unknown is a linear function of the unit fields' solves, each stopped at the CG's tolerance [guess: float32's worst stays under 1.5e-3 with the bodies close; the closest first draw reached 9.4e-4]

gate_1_return_path_redrawn.metric: the largest relative difference over the field and every partner's unknowns

control.plant: drop: the last partner dropped from the elimination; cross: every partner's rows read only its own deliveries
control.resolution: derived: within 2.5 cells the other body's unit field read at a body is of the order of a tenth of its own (the projection's dipolar return falls as the cube of the distance, the kernels overlap below two widths), so zeroing the cross terms moves a force by a share far above float32's 2e-3 [guess: not measured per draw]; structural (on or off), not measured with discriminating_range.py

gate_1_return_path_redrawn.if_wrong: a cross miss in float32 at a close pair means the cross terms are weaker than derived there: print the plant's size per draw and widen the line's margin or move the bodies closer
gate_1_return_path_redrawn.cannot_discriminate_if: two bodies that do not read each other: the draw now places them within 2.5 cells
